column2: The full code is about 2,500 lines (mostly the compressed web panel): download robot_otak.ino. Do not upload a file that already contains your token and API keys anywhere public.
Web panel: Jelajah sendiri (pick 5-30 minutes), or Telegram /jelajah 10

the robot drives forward until there is an obstacle about 40 cm ahead, then turns 70-130° in a random direction (using the gyroscope). If it is boxed in or stuck, it backs up and turns around. It stops on its own when the time is up, the battery is down to 10%, the robot tilts, or the STOP button is pressed. The arrow buttons, /biasa, or STOP also end it. Works through the AI too: "go for a walk"
Web panel: the Baterai section, or Telegram /baterai

battery charge in percent, a voltage graph of the last 6 hours (one point per minute), and an estimate of the remaining time from the last half hour. Voice and Telegram warnings at 20% and 10%. The percentage also shows on the screen

Exploring keeps bumping into chair or table legs: the ultrasonic sensor does not see thin objects. When the front distance has not changed for 5 seconds, the robot assumes it is stuck, backs up and turns around. For a room full of chair legs, explore a different room.

Battery percentage moves up and down a few points while the motors run: the voltage dips briefly when the motors draw current. The number is smoothed, but the remaining-time estimate only becomes accurate after 10-30 minutes.
Indonesian male voice (optional)
Microsoft Azure account
Laptop on the same WiFi as the robot

The robot's default voice is Google's (female). For a male voice with an Indonesian accent, Zond uses the Ardi voice (id-ID-ArdiNeural) from Azure Speech. Free for 500,000 characters per month, enough for thousands of sentences.
Sign in to portal.azure.com. Click Create a resource, search for Speech, choose Microsoft's Speech service, then Create.

Fill in: Resource group → Create new, for example zond. Region → Southeast Asia (closest). Name anything, for example zond-suara. Pricing tier → Free F0. Make sure it is F0, not S0: the free tier never bills; when its quota runs out, Azure refuses until the next month. Click Review + create, then Create, and wait until it finishes.
Click Go to resource, then Keys and Endpoint in the left menu. Copy KEY 1 into AZURE_KUNCI, and put the Location/Region (for example southeastasia) into AZURE_WILAYAH in the brain code.
Upload the brain code (over WiFi as in Step 4). Want a female voice with an Indonesian accent? Change AZURE_SUARA to id-ID-GadisNeural.

Type /bilang halo, aku Zond in Telegram. In the web panel (Musik dan suara section) you can switch between the male voice and Google, and see how many characters have been used this month. In Telegram: /suara, /suara google, /suara azure.

Why does it work this way? The brain code sends the sentence to Azure as SSML, receives an MP3, saves it in the S3's flash memory (the same 9.9 MB FATFS partition required for WiFi uploads), then plays it. Because each sentence is downloaded first, the pause before speaking is slightly longer than with the Google voice. If Azure fails, that sentence is spoken right away with the Google voice, so the robot never goes silent.
The robot speaks with a male voice. The Serial Monitor prints lines such as [suara] Azure 640 ms, 1234 huruf bulan ini.
The bot sends "Suara Azure ditolak (kode 401)": the KEY is wrong or swapped with the region. Copy KEY 1 again. The robot retries Azure 10 minutes later, or right after a restart.
Code 403 after a lot of use: this month's free quota is used up. The robot uses the Google voice until the next month.
The Serial Monitor prints Azure gagal (-2) or another negative number: the robot cannot connect to Azure. Check AZURE_WILAYAH (lowercase without spaces, e.g. southeastasia) and the WiFi.
The Serial Monitor prints penyimpanan flash TIDAK ADA: the Partition Scheme is still Huge APP. Change it to 16M Flash (3MB APP/9.9MB FATFS) and upload over USB.
Send /jelajah 2: the robot drives on its own for 2 minutes, turning whenever it meets an obstacle. Keep your hand near the STOP button.
